title: Mechanisms of Linguistic Change
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.translation: 大規模且有規律的變化通常稱為甚麼？

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph B

sections.title: Skim 時，Paragraph B 首句已經說

blocks.text: “When we study the pronunciation of a language over any period of a few generations or more, we find there are always large-scale regularities in the changes…”
中文意思：
當我們研究一種語言在幾代或更長時間內的發音時，會發現變化中總是有大規模規律。
Scan 時，題目定位詞是 Large-scale regular changes。原文對應句是：
“Such regular changes are often called sound laws.”
中文意思：
這類有規律的變化通常稱為 sound laws。
● Large-scale regular changes = Such regular changes● are usually called = are often called● 答案詞 = sound laws所以答案是 sound laws。字數是兩個詞，符合 NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS。

questions.prompt: “First, one person may imitate another’s pronunciation, especially that of a person with prestige, so imitation involves an element of 28 ______.”
questions.translation: 第一，一個人可能模仿另一個人的發音，尤其是有 prestige 的人的發音，因此 imitation 含有甚麼元素？

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph C Paragraph C 首句：
“It is also possible that fashion plays a part in the process of change.”
fashion 也可能在變化過程中發揮作用。
Scan 時，題目定位詞是 imitate / prestige。原文中間說：
“It certainly plays a part in the spread of change: one person imitates another, and people with the most prestige are most likely to be imitated…”
它確實在變化的傳播中發揮作用：一個人模仿另一個人，而最有 prestige 的人最可能被模仿。
題目的 “imitation involves an element of…” 對應原文 “fashion plays a part”。這裡的 fashion 不是衣服潮流，而是社會上被視為時髦、有地位、值得模仿的發音方式。
所以答案是 fashion。

questions.prompt: “Second, children’s imitations of adult speech may be 29 ______…”
questions.translation: 第二，兒童對成人 speech 的模仿可能是怎樣的？

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph D Paragraph D 首句：
“A less specific variant of the argument is that children’s imitation is imperfect: they copy their parents’ speech, but never reproduce it exactly.”
這個論點的一個較不具體版本是：兒童的模仿是不完美的；他們模仿父母的 speech，但永遠不會完全複製。
Scan 時，題目詞 children’s imitations 和 adult speech 對應原文 “children’s imitation” 和
“parents’ speech”。答案詞就在冒號前：“children’s imitation is imperfect”
兒童的模仿是不完美的。
題目把 “copy their parents’ speech” 概括成 “imitations of adult speech”，但答案詞不變。
所以答案是 imperfect。

questions.prompt: “Finally, random variations in pronunciation may reflect the 30 ______, or minimisation of effort.”
questions.translation: 最後，發音中的 random variations 可能反映甚麼，也就是 minimisation of effort？

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph E Paragraph E 首句：
“One such force which is often invoked is the principle of ease, or minimization of effort.”
一種常被引用的力量是 principle of ease，也就是 minimization of effort。
Scan 時，題目定位詞是 minimisation of effort。原文幾乎逐字出現 “minimization of effort”，並且在前面給出同位語：
“the principle of ease”
題目空格在 “the ______, or minimisation of effort” 之前，所以要填與 minimisation of effort 同義的完整名詞短語。
所以答案是 principle of ease。字數三個詞，符合限制。

questions.prompt: “It is impossible for modern people to determine the pronunciation of words in an earlier age.”
questions.translation: 現代人不可能判斷早期語言中詞語的發音。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph A Paragraph A 首句：
“The changes that have caused the most disagreement are those in pronunciation.”
最引起爭議的變化是發音方面的變化。
Paragraph A 最後一句：

“These various kinds of evidence, combined with a knowledge of the mechanisms of speech-production, can often give us a very good idea of the pronunciation of an earlier age, though absolute certainty is never possible.”
這些不同種類的證據，加上對 speech-production mechanisms 的認識，通常可以讓我們對早期發音有很好的概念，雖然絕對確定永遠不可能。
Scan 時，題目定位詞是 impossible 和 earlier age。原文真正控制答案的是：
“can often give us a very good idea”
題目說 modern people 不可能 determine earlier pronunciation；原文說研究者通常 可以得到很好的概念。雖然原文補充 “absolute certainty is never possible”，但這只是說不能達到百分百確定，不等於完全無法判斷。
● 題目：impossible to determine● 原文：can often give us a very good idea● 題目把「不能絕對確定」放大成「完全不可能判斷」所以答案是 FALSE。

questions.prompt: “A major change in Russian pronunciation was related to changes in the status of social groups.”
questions.translation: 俄語發音中的一項重要變化，和社會群體地位變化有關。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph C Paragraph C 首句：
“It is also possible that fashion plays a part in the process of change.”
fashion 也可能參與變化過程。
Paragraph C 中間有關鍵句：
“When a social group rises or falls in status, its pronunciation may also gain or lose prestige.”
當某個社會群體的地位上升或下降時，它的發音也可能獲得或失去 prestige。
緊接著原文說：
“In Russian, a pronunciation formerly considered desirable later became an undesirable accent, so people tried to disguise it.”
在俄語中，一種以前被視為 desirable 的發音，後來變成 undesirable accent，所以人們試圖掩飾它。
這兩句要合起來讀。前一句建立一般規則：social group status 的升跌會影響 pronunciation 的prestige。後一句馬上給 Russian example：某種俄語發音由 desirable 變成 undesirable，甚至令人要 disguise it。
題目中的 “related to changes in the status of social groups” 對應原文 “When a social group rises or falls in status”。
題目中的 “Russian pronunciation” 對應原文 “In Russian, a pronunciation…”
“major” 雖然不是原文字眼，但 “formerly considered desirable later became an undesirable accent” 是明顯的社會評價逆轉，足以支援題目所說的 significant change。所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “Children learn speech from adults but do not reproduce it exactly.”
questions.translation: 兒童從成人身上學 speech，但不會完全複製。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph D Paragraph D 首句：
“A less specific variant of the argument is that children’s imitation is imperfect: they copy their parents’ speech, but never reproduce it exactly.”
這個論點的一個較不具體版本是：兒童的模仿是不完美的；他們模仿父母的 speech，但永遠不會完全複製。

這題幾乎是原文直接改寫：● Children learn speech from adults = they copy their parents’ speech● do not reproduce it exactly = never reproduce it exactly● adults = parents 是成人中的具體例子原文下一句 “This is true” 也確認作者接受這個描述。
所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “Casual inaccuracies in pronunciation will not have a major influence on language change.”
questions.translation: 偶然、隨機的發音不準，不會對語言變化造成重大影響。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph D Paragraph D 最後一句：

“This, however, cannot explain changes in pronunciation unless it can be shown that there is some systematic trend in the failures of imitation: if they are merely random deviations they will cancel one another out and there will be no net change in the language.”
不過，這不能解釋發音變化，除非能證明 imitation failures 中有某種系統性趨勢；如果它們只是random deviations，它們會互相抵消，語言中不會出現淨變化。
Scan 時，題目定位詞是 casual inaccuracies。原文對應的是：
“merely random deviations”
題目中的 “will not have a major influence on language change” 對應原文：
“they will cancel one another out and there will be no net change in the language”
也就是說，隨機偏差會抵消，不能形成真正的語言變化。只有 systematic trend 才可能帶來change。
所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “The word scant can be pronounced more easily than skamt.”
questions.translation: scant 比 skamt 更容易發音。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph E Paragraph E 首句：
“One such force which is often invoked is the principle of ease, or minimization of effort.”
一種常被引用的力量是 principle of ease，也就是 minimization of effort。
原文關鍵句：
“For example, the word scant was once skamt, but the /m/ has been changed to /n/ under the influence of the following /t/. Greater efficiency has hereby been achieved…”
例如，scant 這個詞曾經是 skamt，但 /m/ 受後面 /t/ 的影響變成 /n/。這樣就達到了更高效率。
後面解釋原因：
“because /n/ and /t/ are articulated in the same place…”
因為 /n/ 和 /t/ 在同一個位置發音。

題目說 “can be pronounced more easily”，原文說 “Greater efficiency has hereby been achieved”。這是直接同義改寫：● more easily = with greater efficiency / less effort● scant = /n/ before /t/● skamt = /m/ before /t/由於 /n/ 和 /t/ 發音位置相同，scant 的發音比 skamt 更有效率。
所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “The silent [g] in gnat will eventually disappear from its spelling.”
questions.translation: gnat 中不發音的 [g] 最終會從拼寫中消失。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph F Paragraph F 首句：
“Assimilation is not the only way in which we change our pronunciation in order to increase efficiency.”
assimilation 不是我們為了提高效率而改變發音的唯一方法。
Paragraph F 中間說：
“At one time there was a [t] in words like castle and Christmas, and an initial [k] in words like knight and know.”
曾經，castle 和 Christmas 這類詞中有 [t] 音；knight 和 know 這類詞開頭有 [k] 音。
題目定位詞是 silent [g] in gnat 和 disappear from its spelling。原文確實談到拼寫與發音不完全一致的例子，例如 castle、Christmas、knight、know，但沒有提到：● gnat；● silent [g]；● spelling will eventually change；● 某個字母會從拼寫中消失。
原文只說 pronunciation 中某些 consonants 消失或不再讀出，沒有預測 future spelling change。
題目加入了未來拼寫變化，原文沒有提供。
所以答案是 NOT GIVEN。

questions.prompt: “The pronunciation of temporary does not always reflect its full spelling.”
questions.translation: temporary 的發音不一定完整反映它的拼寫。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph F Paragraph F 最後一句：

“Sometimes a whole syllable is dropped out when two successive syllables begin with the same consonant (haplology): a recent example is temporary, which in Britain is often pronounced as if it were tempory.”
有時候，當連續兩個 syllables 以相同 consonant 開頭時，整個 syllable 會被省略，這叫haplology；近代例子是 temporary，在英國常被讀成像 tempory。
題目中的 “does not always reflect its full spelling” 對應原文：
“often pronounced as if it were tempory”
temporary 的拼寫比 tempory 多一個 syllable 感覺；原文說英國常見發音會省略其中一部分，所以發音不一定完整反映 spelling。
注意題目用 “not always”，語氣很保守。原文用 “often pronounced as if…” 也支援這種保守說法。
所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.answer: C — A large-scale trend in pronunciation over a given period
questions.answerKey: C — A large-scale trend in pronunciation over a given period
questions.prompt: “As a consequence, ‘b’ will be pronounced as ‘p’”
questions.translation: 結果是，b 會被讀成 p。

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph B原文關鍵句：
“…all the [b] consonants in a certain position (for example at the end of a word) may change into [p] consonants.”
在某個位置上的所有 [b] consonants，例如在詞尾，可能會變成 [p] consonants。
這句前面說的是：
“large-scale regularities in the changes”
變化中的大規模規律。
後面說：
“Such regular changes are often called sound laws.”
這類規律性變化通常稱為 sound laws。
因此，b 變 p 的例子不是單一發音錯誤，也不是某一個詞的偶然簡化；它屬於某個語言或方言在特定時期出現的大規模發音趨勢。
所以答案是 C。

questions.answer: B — Assimilation of a sound under the influence of a neighbouring one
questions.answerKey: B — Assimilation of a sound under the influence of a neighbouring one

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph E原文先定義 assimilation：
“Assimilation is the changing of a sound under the influence of a neighbouring one.”
Assimilation 是一個 sound 受到鄰近 sound 影響而改變。
接著給出 scant 的例子：
“For example, the word scant was once skamt, but the /m/ has been changed to /n/ under the influence of the following /t/.”
例如，scant 曾經是 skamt，但 /m/ 受後面 /t/ 的影響變成 /n/。
題目的 [mt] → [nt] 正是這個例子：● /m/ changes to /n/；● following /t/ 是 neighbouring sound；● under the influence of the following /t/ = under the influence of a neighbouring one。
選項 D 也和這個例子有關，因為原文確實解釋 /n/ 和 /t/ 在同一位置發音。不過 Q39 的句子問的是這種 sound change 屬於哪種機制；B 直接命名為 assimilation，因此最貼合。
所以答案是 B。

questions.answer: A — The speaker can pronounce it with less effort
questions.answerKey: A — The speaker can pronounce it with less effort
questions.prompt: “The omission of ‘t’ from the pronunciation of Christmas”

blocks.text: 目標段落：Paragraph F Paragraph F 首句：
“Assimilation is not the only way in which we change our pronunciation in order to increase efficiency.”
assimilation 不是我們為了提高效率而改變發音的唯一方法。
接著原文說：
“Consonant clusters are often simplified. At one time there was a [t] in words like castle and Christmas…”
consonant clusters 常常被簡化。曾經，castle 和 Christmas 這類詞中有 [t] 音。
這裡的 Christmas 省略 [t] 屬於 consonant cluster simplification。Paragraph F 的大框架是
“increase efficiency”，即用更少 effort 發音。因此選項 A “The speaker can pronounce it with less effort” 最合適。
● omission of ‘t’ = consonant cluster simplified● pronounce with less effort = increase efficiency● Christmas = 原文直接例子所以答案是 A。

paragraphOverview.title: Skim Roadmap：全文段落地圖
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: 只看首句和尾句，可以看到本段處理「過去發音如何被重建」。首句說最有爭議的語言變化是pronunciation changes；尾句說多種證據配合 speech-production knowledge，通常能讓我們對earlier pronunciation 有很好的概念，但 absolute certainty 永遠不可能。這段功能是介紹歷史發音研究的證據來源與限制：可以推得相當可靠，仍未達到絕對確定。

首句說，只要研究一種語言幾代以上的 pronunciation，就會發現 large-scale regularities。尾句說沒有 universal sound laws，只有特定語言或方言在特定時期的 particular sound laws。這段功能是定義和限制 “sound laws”：它們描述大規模、規律性的發音變化，例如 long [a:] 變成 long [e:]，或 word-final [b] 變成 [p]。

首句直接提出 fashion 可能參與 change；最後一句說十七、十八世紀 accepted English pronunciation 的一些變化，可能源於當時 middle classes 權力和財富上升，並逐步影響upper-class speech。這段功能是說明社會因素如何推動發音變化：人會模仿有 prestige 的人或群體，社會地位升跌會影響某種 pronunciation 的 prestige。
首句說，有一種較不具體的說法：children’s imitation is imperfect。尾句說，如果 imitation failures只是 random deviations，它們會互相抵消，語言不會有 net change。這段功能是評估「模仿不完美」是否能解釋發音變化。作者承認兒童和成人發音會有偏差，但強調只有 systematic trend 才可能帶來真正語言變化。

首句提出一種常被引用的力量：principle of ease, or minimization of effort。最後一句用 football pronounced as foopball 作近代例子。這段功能是介紹 assimilation：一個 sound 受 neighbouring sound 影響而改變，使 articulation 更有效率。scant 由 skamt 變來，因 /n/ 和 /t/ 發音位置相同，比 /m/ 接 /t/ 更省力。

首句說 assimilation 並非唯一提升發音效率的方法；最後一句說 temporary 在英國常被讀成tempory，這屬於 haplology 的近例。這段功能是列出其他 simplification：word-final consonants可消失，consonant clusters 可簡化，whole syllable 也可能被刪去。castle、Christmas、knight、know 和 temporary 都是拼寫保留較多，實際發音較簡化的例子。
